userStories.title: A brief claim stranded by a worker that died is taken over, so the day still gets its one brief
userStories.description: As a person, I want the day's brief even when the worker that claimed it died before posting, so that a deploy or a crash mid-build never leaves me with no brief and an open that answers pending all day (PRD-268 §6.4, K11; W2 review finding, raised by the code-reviewer, the security-reviewer and the database-reviewer).
acceptanceCriteria: Cause: claim_brief (services/mobile/digest.py claim, :249-259) commits the mobile_digest_posts row before the build, and only a raised error or a post that does not land gives it back (services/brief/on_open.py open_brief; digest._post_or_release). A process killed between the claim and the post (a Railway deploy or restart, an OOM kill, a connection lost during generate_digest's model call) leaves the row and no message. Every later open that day then takes the lost-claim path, todays_brief_message finds nothing, and the route answers {posted: false, pending: true} until the local date ends; the scheduled tick (_serve_workspace) counts it TAKEN and posts nothing; the web never retries a pending answer in the tab. on_open._give_back logging a failed release without retrying strands the day the same way. Change: the claim becomes a lease on its existing posted_at column (server_default now(), NOT NULL; core/models/mobile_push.py:81), with no new column and no migration, so K6 and K11 hold. A new setting BRIEF_CLAIM_STALE_SECONDS in orchestrator/config.py (name in reports/config-surface.json; default 600, and longer than the build's longest model call: read the LLM client's timeout in core/llm and say it in the comment). A claimant that loses the INSERT and finds no day's message takes the claim over with one committed compare-and-set: UPDATE mobile_digest_posts SET posted_at = now() WHERE workspace_id, user_id and local_date are the person's AND posted_at < now() - the stale interval RETURNING posted_at, with bound parameters. The one claimant whose UPDATE returns a row builds and posts as the winner; every other claimant answers as today. One helper beside claim and release in services/mobile/digest.py, used by both open_brief (via open) and _serve_workspace (via schedule) → DONE — commit f15bfa624. services/mobile/digest.py: lease (INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING posted_at, committed; claim is now lease(...) is not None, same bool), take_over (one committed compare-and-set: UPDATE mobile_digest_posts SET posted_at = now() WHERE the person's workspace_id, user_id, local_date AND posted_at < now() - BRIEF_CLAIM_STALE_SECONDS RETURNING posted_at; ORM update() with bound parameters), the helper beside claim and release that both paths use: open_brief via on_open._hold (lease, else the day's message, else take_over) and _serve_workspace via digest._hold (the same; todays_brief_message imported at first use, as services.brief.claim imports digest). config.BRIEF_CLAIM_STALE_SECONDS default 600 (floor 60), in reports/config-surface.json; its comment names the clients' timeouts: OpenAI-compatible 180 s per try + the SDK's two retries = 540 s; the Anthropic client (the platform default) sets none, so its SDK's 600 s per try and two retries hold. JUDGEMENT FOR GERARD: the AC asks for 600 AND longer than the longest call; 600 does not outlast the Anthropic SDK's own timeout, so 600 was kept (the AC's number) and the comment says so; a taken-over slow winner posts nothing (AC 2), so the cost is a second build, never a second brief. No column, no migration (K6, K11 hold). services/brief/since.py last_brief_at is unchanged: a taken-over claim keeps its local_date, so its read of max(posted_at) over earlier dates still sees the day; posted_at now ends at the pre-post stamp (AC 2), the moment of the post, rather than the first INSERT. Flags (open calls, not built): a day whose message the person deleted is taken over and posted again once the claim is stale (once per stale interval); the scheduled path now reads todays_brief_message whenever a tick loses the INSERT (messages has no chat_id index; an index needs a migration this wave forbids); digest.claim and claim.claim_brief stay as the bool claim the unchanged tests call, with no production caller left

A winner whose lease was taken over never posts: claiming and taking over each give back the posted_at the claimant holds; just before the post the winner re-reads its row and posts only while posted_at still equals it, else it logs by class only and answers as a lost claim (open: the day's message or pending; schedule: TAKEN). release gains an optional keyword for the posted_at the releaser holds, and with it deletes only that row, so a slow winner that fails after a takeover never deletes the taker's claim. Callers that pass no keyword behave exactly as today, and the PRD-266 digest tests are unchanged → DONE — commit f15bfa624. digest.still_held, just before the post: UPDATE … SET posted_at = clock_timestamp() WHERE the person's key AND posted_at = :held RETURNING posted_at, committed, else LeaseLost. JUDGEMENT: the re-read is a compare-and-set that re-stamps the lease (clock_timestamp, not now(): the open path's build runs its model call inside the session's transaction), so no takeover can land between the look and the message commit (find_or_create_auto_chat commits mid-delivery, so a FOR UPDATE lock would not hold through the insert); a taker racing it waits on the row and finds it fresh. digest.post_held_brief (claim.post_brief(..., held=)) gives back the stamped claim itself when the delivery does not land or raises. No keyword deletes as today: the PRD-266 digest tests are unchanged.
